=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66; Tool Access live 157/159, template 168/170) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The new "One log PR per session" bullet requires opening a draft PR, checking its state and marking it ready for review. The Tool Access section still says `gh` never mutates and that the issue-comment tick is the one GitHub write, and the diff did not update it.
  WHY: A session that follows the declared Tool Access stalls or refuses the PR step. A session that follows the bullet exceeds its declared capabilities. Reviewers rated this MAJOR, which this ledger maps to high.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:55-59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:62,66) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The earlier-session log PR is only looked for "before your first log commit". The read-first rule says to read the log before emitting any step, so the session can resume from a stale default-branch log.
  WHY: The session re-emits steps that are already done, and the later merge can conflict with its local log edits. Reviewers rated this MAJOR, which this ledger maps to high.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66; Rules live ~170-171, template ~181-182) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The detection predicate requires the earlier log PR to change only `docs/deploy-activation/`. The Rules require ID records in the agents file or `agents.d/` to be pushed in the same push as the log.
  WHY: A log PR that carries an ID record is not recognised. The session opens a second log PR and the recorded IDs are stranded. The reviewers' severity was NIT, which this ledger maps to low.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The rule gives no failure path when merging the earlier session's branch fails, for example on conflicts in `docs/deploy-activation/*.md`.
  WHY: The session has to improvise, so its behaviour is non-deterministic. The reviewers' severity was NIT, which this ledger maps to low.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The check of the PR's state and the `git push` are not atomic, so a merge between them lands the push on a branch whose PR has already merged.
  WHY: The window is small and the next session's state check recovers from it. The reviewers' severity was NIT, which this ledger maps to low.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The new bullet does not name the repository (`THIS_REPO` or `-R <owner>/<repo>`), unlike the neighbouring template bullets at lines 61, 62 and 65.
  WHY: A PR opened or looked up without a named repository can target the wrong one. The reviewers' severity was NIT, which this ledger maps to low.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fixed PR title `chore: activation log updates` carries no project reference.
  WHY: Reviewers cannot map merged log PRs to projects without opening each one. The reviewers' severity was NIT, which this ledger maps to low.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The PR description says the Activation Log section of both command copies and `docs/deploy-activation/README.md` implement the "One log PR per session" rule, with nothing deferred. The rule requires opening a draft PR, checking its state and marking it ready.
  expected_change_site: `## Tool Access` and `## Rules` of `.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md` (lines 152-161) and `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md` (lines 163-172)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The diff changes only the Activation Log bullets, the README paragraph, the changelog fragment and the new test. Tool Access (live lines 157 and 159) still says `gh` is never used to mutate and calls the issue-comment tick the one GitHub write. No hunk touches `## Tool Access` or `## Rules` in either copy.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md; read-first bullet at live line 55 / template line 62) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The earlier-session log PR is only discovered at "before your first log commit", although the read-first bullet says to read the log before emitting any step.
  WHY: The session can read an older copy and re-emit steps that are already `[x]` on the earlier PR's branch, then hit a merge conflict on the same log file.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The detection predicate requires the earlier PR to change only `docs/deploy-activation/`, but the Rules (live about 170-171, template about 181-182) push ID records to the agents file in the same push as the log.
  WHY: A log PR carrying an ID record is not recognised, so a second log PR is opened and the IDs are not carried over.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The PR-state check and the `git push` are not atomic.
  WHY: A merge between them lands the push on an already merged PR's branch. The window is small and the next session's state check recovers from it.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The rule gives no instruction for a failed merge of the earlier branch.
  WHY: The session has to improvise, so behaviour differs between sessions.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The new bullet does not name the repository (`THIS_REPO` or `-R <owner>/<repo>`), unlike the bullets at lines 61, 62 and 65.
  WHY: A PR opened or looked up without a named repo can target the wrong one.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:157,159 (template Tool Access about 168-170) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Opening a PR and marking it ready are GitHub writes that the declared Tool Access scope forbids, and neither `## Tool Access` nor `## Rules` was updated.
  WHY: The declared capabilities no longer match what the command does, so one-PR-per-session behaviour is unreliable.
- TASK_GAP: (task gap, severity=MAJOR, confidence=3)
  Requirement: The PR description says both command copies and `docs/deploy-activation/README.md` implement the "One log PR per session" rule, and nothing is deferred. The rule requires opening a draft PR and marking it ready.
  Expected change site: The `## Tool Access` section (and the matching `## Rules` bullets) of both command copies. A bullet there should allow draft PR creation, PR state reads and the ready-for-review transition, limited to the log PR and never used to merge or close.
  Evidence of absence: The diff changes only the Activation Log bullets, the README paragraph, the changelog fragment and the new test. Live line 157 still says `gh` is never used to mutate, and live line 159 still calls the issue-comment tick the only GitHub write.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: add one Tool Access bullet per file (about 2 lines) allowing the log-PR writes only and naming `THIS_REPO`; extend `tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py::test_one_session_keeps_its_log_updates_in_one_pull_request` to assert it (about 3 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66; read-first at line 55/62) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The earlier open log PR is checked "before your first log commit", but the read-first rule requires reading the log before emitting any step.
  WHY: A session may read a stale log and repeat work already done, then conflict when merging the earlier branch.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: No failure or recovery path is defined if `git merge` of the earlier session's log PR branch fails.
  WHY: The agent's behaviour becomes non-deterministic on a conflict, so it may stall or open a new PR incorrectly.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The detection predicate requires only `docs/deploy-activation/` changes, but the "Persistence" rule requires agents-file or `agents.d/` ID-recording pushes in the same push as the log.
  WHY: A log PR with agents-file updates is not recognised, so a second conflicting log PR is opened.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fixed PR title `chore: activation log updates` lacks a project-specific reference.
  WHY: Reviewers cannot map merged log PRs to projects without opening each one.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh` operations (checking PR state, opening draft PRs, merging branches) are not declared in the `Interaction Protocol` or `Tool Access` section.
  WHY: An agent following its declared Tool Access sees them as unauthorized, so it stalls or refuses.
- TASK_GAP: (task gap, severity=MAJOR, confidence=3)
  Requirement: The PR description says the Activation Log section of both command copies and docs/deploy-activation/README.md implement the One log PR per session rule.
  Expected change site: The `## Tool Access` and `## Rules` sections of both command copies.
  Evidence of absence: The diff only touches the Activation Log bullets, the README paragraph and the new test. Those sections still say the only permitted GitHub write is the issue-comment tick and that `gh` is never used to mutate.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66; read-first at live line 55 / template line 62) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge of the earlier session's branch is gated to "before your first log commit", not to read-first time, so a session reads the stale default-branch log first.
  WHY: The session advances past steps the earlier session already completed and has to back out when the merge lands. This breaks the Activation Log's resume contract in the multi-session case.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template line 66; Rules live lines 170-171 / template lines 181-182) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The detection predicate excludes any earlier log PR that also touches `agents.md` or `agents.d/`, although the Rules require ID records in the same push as the log.
  WHY: The predicate never matches, so the earlier session's IDs are stranded on a closed log PR and a second log PR opens.
